text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bund futures end higher with help from other European bond markets. Market focused on Ecofin meeting this weekend and next week's Fed meeting. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 98.28, up 0.21 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts held fast to slender gains but under- performed Bunds as the market speculated on outcome of this weekend's Dublin Ecofin summit regarding stability pact and if UK would be left behind. Monday's monetary meeting keeps gilts on their toes. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 107-20/32, up 04/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures settle near new contract high hit today. Traders said good cash demand from non-residents, mood bullish. PIBOR buoyed by franc strength, call money cut. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 124.20 up 0.28 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to higher levels helped by the steady lira, firmer bunds and against a background of hopes of lower inflation and lower interest rates. Concern over the 1997 financial budget briefly worries BTPs, but the market mood was generally positive. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 118.79 up 0.67 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries remain stuck in narrow range, little changed in data sparse session. Volume extremely light. Positioning ahead of Tuesday's FOMC meeting seen dictating trade. Slim majority seen leaning toward 25 bp Fed hike. Talk regional Fed banks pressuring for rate hike continues.The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-25/32, up 04/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.04 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Tokyo easier on Friday due to corrective selling after sharp gains on Thursday, traders said. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.10, up 0.03 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Westpac Banking Corp launched a $500 million five-year FRN at three-month LIBOR flat in a relatively slow end to the week. The bank is rated AA3 by Moody's Investors Service and AA- by Standard & Poor's Corp. Joint lead managers were HSBC Markets and Morgan Stanley were not immediately available for comment. AA3/AA- rated Ontario issued a A$125 million five-year discount bond which pays a five percent coupon via Daiwa Europe.
